pharm: Potent synthetic glucocorticoid that binds intracellular corticosteroid receptors to modulate gene transcription, producing broad anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects with negligible mineralocorticoid activity.
quick: Oral forms: take with food to limit GI upset
Use if benefit outweighs risk; used antenatally for fetal lung maturity
Glucose, blood pressure, infection, adrenal suppression
summary: Betamethasone is a potent, long-acting synthetic glucocorticoid with minimal mineralocorticoid activity, used systemically (oral or by intramuscular, intra-articular, intralesional, and soft-tissue injection of the sodium phosphate/acetate suspension) for a wide range of allergic, dermatologic, rheumatic, hematologic, endocrine, and other inflammatory and immune disorders. Antenatally it accelerates fetal lung maturity in threatened preterm birth. Prolonged use risks adrenal suppression, hyperglycemia, immunosuppression, osteoporosis, and Cushingoid effects; do not stop abruptly after extended therapy.
indications: Severe or incapacitating allergic conditions (e.g., asthma, contact/atopic dermatitis, serum sickness, drug hypersensitivity, allergic rhinitis)
Dermatologic, rheumatic, and collagen (e.g., SLE) inflammatory disorders
Endocrine disorders including adrenocortical insufficiency (with mineralocorticoid) and congenital adrenal hyperplasia
Hematologic, gastrointestinal (e.g., ulcerative colitis), respiratory, ophthalmic, edematous (nephrotic), and neoplastic conditions responsive to corticosteroids
Local injection for inflammatory joint, bursal, and soft-tissue conditions; antenatal use to promote fetal lung maturity in preterm labor

dosage.d: 0.25-9 mg/day of betamethasone sodium phosphate/acetate suspension depending on the condition
Large joints 1-2 mL; small joints 0.25-0.5 mL; bursae 0.25-2 mL of suspension
dosage.n: Limit frequency of repeated joint injections

dosage.d: 12 mg IM, two doses 24 hours apart (per obstetric protocol)
Taper gradually rather than stopping abruptly
dosage.n: Avoid adrenal crisis from abrupt withdrawal

admin: For the injectable suspension, do not administer intravenously; give by IM, intra-articular, intralesional, or soft-tissue injection as indicated
Use preservative-free preparations for neonates/premature infants (benzyl alcohol gasping syndrome)
Take oral forms with food to reduce gastrointestinal irritation
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration
Taper gradually when discontinuing after prolonged therapy
moa: Betamethasone diffuses across cell membranes and binds cytoplasmic glucocorticoid receptors; the complex translocates to the nucleus and alters transcription of genes encoding inflammatory mediators. This suppresses production of cytokines, prostaglandins, and leukotrienes, stabilizes lysosomal membranes, reduces capillary permeability and leukocyte migration, and broadly dampens immune and inflammatory responses. It has high glucocorticoid potency and a long duration with essentially no sodium-retaining (mineralocorticoid) activity.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to betamethasone or formulation components
Administration of live or live-attenuated vaccines while on immunosuppressive doses
Intramuscular use in idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura
relative: Osteoporosis, psychiatric disorders, ocular herpes simplex, glaucoma

preg: Corticosteroids cross the placenta; use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the risk. Antenatal betamethasone is used deliberately to accelerate fetal lung maturity in threatened preterm birth. Monitor neonates exposed late in pregnancy for hypoadrenalism.
lact: Systemic corticosteroids are excreted in human milk and could suppress growth or endogenous steroid production in the infant; use with caution and monitor the breastfed infant.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment; use the lowest effective dose and monitor for fluid retention and blood pressure.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; corticosteroid effects may be enhanced. No standard numeric dose adjustment is specified.

major: Live vaccines - contraindicated at immunosuppressive doses (risk of disseminated infection)
CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, ritonavir) - increase corticosteroid exposure
moderate: CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, phenytoin, phenobarbital) - reduce corticosteroid efficacy
Potassium-depleting diuretics and amphotericin B - additive hypokalemia
minor: Skin test reactions may be suppressed
interactions.food: Take oral forms with food to reduce gastric irritation.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; additive risk of gastrointestinal irritation/ulceration.
interactions.diagnostics: May suppress reactions to skin tests; can elevate blood glucose and suppress HPA-axis testing (e.g., cosyntropin response).

serious: HPA-axis (adrenal) suppression and adrenal crisis on withdrawal
Increased susceptibility to and masking of infection
emergency: Adrenal crisis (after abrupt withdrawal or stress)

monitoring: Body weight, fluid status, and electrolytes (potassium)
Bone density and growth (children) with prolonged use
Ocular pressure/cataracts; signs of adrenal suppression
counsel: Do not stop this medicine suddenly after taking it for a long time - the dose must be reduced slowly
Carry a steroid alert card; you may need extra steroid during illness, injury, or surgery
Take oral doses with food to protect your stomach
Report signs of infection, severe stomach pain, black stools, or mood changes
Avoid contact with chickenpox or measles if you are not immune, and avoid live vaccines
pk: Phosphate salt acts rapidly; acetate salt provides prolonged effect
Long-acting; biologic effect up to ~36-72 hours
Store at 20-25 C; do not freeze; protect from light (per labeling)
pearls: Long-acting, high-potency glucocorticoid with negligible mineralocorticoid effect
Never stop abruptly after prolonged use - taper to prevent adrenal crisis; give stress dosing for illness/surgery
Injectable sodium phosphate/acetate suspension is for IM/local injection, not IV
Antenatal betamethasone (12 mg IM x2, 24 h apart) accelerates fetal lung maturity in preterm labor
Use preservative-free formulations in neonates (benzyl alcohol gasping syndrome)
missed: For regular oral therapy, take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose; do not double up. Do not stop on your own. For scheduled injections, follow your clinician's instructions.
overdose: Acute overdose of corticosteroids is rarely life-threatening; chronic excess produces Cushingoid features, fluid retention, hyperglycemia, hypertension, and immunosuppression. Management is supportive and includes gradual dose reduction; monitor electrolytes, glucose, and blood pressure, and watch for adrenal suppression.
